rivals.statement: Accuracy is capped by the share of problems whose solution the model can finish within its per-sample token budget. The autobench method caps each of its 12 T 0.6 samples at 4,096 tokens. Voting fixes problems that are already within reach, but the 10-15 % of MATH-500 problems whose base solutions run past about 4,000 tokens get no complete sample, so no vote can get them right. Raising a cap pays exactly where answers were being cut off, not elsewhere.
rivals.readers_wrong: The readers priced a vote over 12 like the cued base's T 1.0 vote over 12 at a 16,384 cap (466/500, 93 %). The 4,096 cap removes the long tail before any vote, so the method stays at its dev level of about 84 % (338/400).

holds_against.why: The plain base at T 0.6 hits the 16,384 cap 65 times, mostly in loops, so a higher cap might buy nothing. But the plain p95 finished length is 4,876 tokens (knowledge-0b450e), so the 4,096 cap also cuts finished non-loop solutions that a vote could use.

On the 328 the method is only 6.4 points below one cued sample, a smaller gap than a pure length ceiling suggests. The cued sample also loses 77 answers to its own 16,384 cap, so both arms are length-limited on the 328.

forecasts.reason: Think-SFT cue at 32k gives 230-235 over 4 seeds; the native template keeps the same length profile, so the cap still binds the same way.
The cue's 16k view averages 210.8; the cap removes about 24 answers that finish late.
Think-SFT cue MATH-500 is 457-462 at 16k with 25 cap hits; at 32k nearly all of them finish and about 40 % are right.
Same answers counted at 16k, matching the stored 16k cue singles.
The template changes the register, not the length budget; paired difference near 0 with one-sample noise of about 8.
At 16k both arms lose the same long tail.
The cued base at a 16,384 cap is rarely cut off on MATH-500; preliminary votes over 8 and 12 are 458 and 466, so 9 interpolates.
The base hits the cap on about 23 % of samples on the 328; pass@4 is 207, so the vote over 8 stays below about 207.
The vote over 3 is 246; a fourth sample adds little once cap hits (about 40) set the ceiling.
a=1 scores 467; MATH-500 is rarely cut off, so a=2 changes little.
M(2) at 16k is 229-237 with about 40 cap hits; at 32k about half finish right, but fewer than for Think-SFT because M(2) already finishes earlier.
Same as t26 with another seed.
Think-SFT gets 234 at 32k on the sample-1 seed; M(2) finishes more of its long answers within 32k, so its edge stays small.
The vote over 4 at the 16k view is 75 with 46 % cap hits; at 32k most cut answers finish (hard328 32k singles +7 points), so the vote gains more than the 328's +6.

rivals.statement: At T 0.6 in the plain register, the base's wrong answers on a problem repeat across samples: low temperature sends draws to the same attractor value. Votes over such samples saturate after a few draws, at the share of problems whose modal answer is right. The token cap is not what binds: long plain samples at T 0.6 are mostly loops. Vote gains need diverse errors, which comes with T 1.0 or the cue's deliberative register.
rivals.readers_wrong: The readers assumed each extra sample in the vote over 12 kept adding accuracy, as at T 1.0 with the cue (446, 458, 466 at 4, 8, 12). The plain T 0.6 vote had already plateaued at its dev level of 84 %, so the 400 gave 338, not 356-362.

holds_against.why: At T 0.6 a vote over 4 of cued samples lifts singles of about 383 to 441, a large vote gain. Most of that lift recovers loop cap hits (85-99 per sample), not repeated finished errors, and it stops at 441 in both arms.
On dev the kept method rose from 61 to 84. That fits early saturation: the gain arrives in the first few draws, and the 400 measured the same 84.5 % plateau.

cell.cap: 8,192 generated tokens; the same answers also scored with every answer longer than 4,096 tokens counted as no answer

cell.command: uv run tools/gpu.py submit l40s --hours 2 -- "bash studies/rlneurons/jobs/setup_vllm.sh && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.theory.jobs.free_cell --model base --set math500 --n 100 --temperature 0.6 --top-p 1.0 --samples 6 --max-tokens 8192 --seed 71000000 --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD)"
cell.readout: From answers.jsonl: vote-over-6 right answers at cap 8,192 minus vote-over-6 right answers when every sample with more than 4,096 generated tokens is treated as giving no answer (same text, paired by problem).
cell.unit: right answers of 100 (difference, 8,192 view minus 4,096 view)
cell.why: Mechanism a says the 4,096 cap removes complete long solutions, so raising it lifts the vote. Mechanism b says long plain T 0.6 samples are loops or repeated wrong values, so the vote barely moves.
